input.chapter_briefing: Carl Manfred's mansion in Detroit, morning. Carl, a famous elderly painter who uses a wheelchair, is cared for by his android, Markus. The grand house is full of art, a piano, a chess set and books. Carl is warm, sharp and blunt, treats Markus as more than a machine and invites him to paint for the first time. His son Leo, a resentful drug user, sometimes turns up asking for money. Stakes: Carl's well-being and Markus's sense of himself.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I'm not programmed to criticize art, I-  You would be a much better judge than I would.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: The truth is I have nothing left to say anymore… Each day that goes by brings me closer to the end… I'm just an old man clinging to his brushes…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl...

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: But enough about me... Let's see if you have any talent! Give it a try. Try painting something.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Paint? But, what I... Painting what?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Anything you want! Give it a try.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: That is a perfect copy, of reality. But painting is not about  replicating the world, it's about interpreting it, improving on it, showing something you see.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl, I don't… think I can do that. It's not in my program… I…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Go on, go, try, grab that canvas. Do something for me, close your eyes.  Close your eyes. Trust me. Try to imagine something that doesn't exist. Something you've never seen. Now, concentrate... on how it makes you feel...  and let your hand drift across the canvas.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Oh my God…

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Hey, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo… I didn't hear you come in...

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I'd stop by… It's been awhile, right?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You all right? You don't look so good.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, I'm fine… Hey listen, uh... I need some cash, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Uh well, it just goes, you know?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Yeah... Yeah, you're on it again, aren't you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: No, no, no, I swear it's not that…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Don't lie to me, Leo.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What difference does it make? I just need some cash, that's all!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Sorry... the answer's no.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What? Why?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You know why.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Yeah, yeah… I think I do know why. You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son, eh? Tell me dad, what's it got that I don't? It’s smarter? More obedient? Not like me, right? But you know what? This thing is not your son.  IT'S A FUCKING MACHINE!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo, that's enough! ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: You don't care about anything except yourself and your goddamn paintings. You've never loved anyone.  You’ve never loved me, Dad…  You never loved me.

dialogue.text: Human emotions are…  intriguing…  Though, I can't really say that I fully understand them.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Humans don't understand them either.  They rule our lives and we have no idea why they make us feel like beggars or kings. Life without emotions wouldn't be worth living.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: One day, I won't be here to take care of you anymore.  You'll have to protect yourself,  and make your choices…  Decide who you are,  and wanna become… This world doesn't like those who are different, Markus.  Don't let anyone tell you who you should be. Let's go to the studio.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Let’s see where we left off… Remove the sheet!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: So...  What's your verdict, Markus?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I'm not programmed to criticize art, I-  You would be a much better judge than I would.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: The truth is I have nothing left to say anymore… Each day that goes by brings me closer to the end… I'm just an old man clinging to his brushes…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl...

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: But enough about me... Let's see if you have any talent! Give it a try. Try painting something.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Paint? But, what I... Painting what?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Anything you want! Give it a try.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: That is a perfect copy, of reality. But painting is not about  replicating the world, it's about interpreting it, improving on it, showing something you see.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Carl, I don't… think I can do that. It's not in my program… I…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Go on, go, try, grab that canvas. Do something for me, close your eyes.  Close your eyes. Trust me. Try to imagine something that doesn't exist. Something you've never seen. Now, concentrate... on how it makes you feel...  and let your hand drift across the canvas.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Oh my God…

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Hey, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo… I didn't hear you come in...

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Ah, I was in the neighborhood… I thought I'd stop by… It's been awhile, right?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You all right? You don't look so good.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Oh, yeah, yeah, I'm fine… Hey listen, uh... I need some cash, Dad.

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Again? What happened to the money I just gave you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Uh well, it just goes, you know?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Yeah... Yeah, you're on it again, aren't you?

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: No, no, no, I swear it's not that…

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Don't lie to me, Leo.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What difference does it make? I just need some cash, that's all!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Sorry... the answer's no.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: What? Why?

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: You know why.

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: Yeah, yeah… I think I do know why. You’d rather take care of your plastic toy here than your own son, eh? Tell me dad, what's it got that I don't? It’s smarter? More obedient? Not like me, right? But you know what? This thing is not your son.  IT'S A FUCKING MACHINE!

dialogue.speaker: Carl
dialogue.text: Leo, that's enough! ENOUGH!

dialogue.speaker: Leo
dialogue.text: You don't care about anything except yourself and your goddamn paintings. You've never loved anyone.  You’ve never loved me, Dad…  You never loved me.

dialogue.speaker: Journalist
dialogue.text: Joss Douglas, for Channel 16. Can you confirm that this is a homicide?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm not confirming anything.

dialogue.speaker: Police android
dialogue.text: Androids are not permitted beyond this point.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: It's with me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What part of ‘stay in the car’ didn’t you understand?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Your order contradicted my instructions, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You don't talk, you don't touch anything and you stay outta my way, got it?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Got it,

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Evening, Hank. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So...  you got yourself an android, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: We had a call around eight from the landlord. The tenant hadn't paid his rent for a few months, so he thought he'd drop by, see what was going on… That’s when he found the body… Jesus, that smell! Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name's Carlos Ortiz. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could've waited 'til morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I'd say he's been there for a good three weeks. We'll know more when the coroner gets here. There's a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Any sign of a break-in?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Nope…  The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must've gone out the back way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about his android?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn't here when we arrived…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I'll be outside if you need me.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant Anderson, my name is Connor. I’m the android sent by CyberLife. I looked for you at the station but nobody knew where you were. They said you were probably having a drink nearby. I was lucky to find you at the fifth bar.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You were assigned a case early this evening. A homicide, involving a CyberLife android. In accordance with procedure, the company has allocated a specialized model to assist investigators.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Well, I don’t need any assistance. Specially not from a plastic asshole like you. So just be a good lil' robot and get the fuck outta here.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'm sorry, Lieutenant, but I must insist. My instructions stipulate that I have to accompany you.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know where you can stick your instructions?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: No... where?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Never mind.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I apologize, Lieutenant. I didn't mean to bother you.  I'll wait for you outside. Take your time.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Did you say homicide?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You wait here. I won't be long.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: My instructions are to accompany you to the crime scene, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Listen, I don’t give a fuck about your instructions. I told you to wait here, so you shut the fuck up  and you wait here.

dialogue.speaker: Journalist
dialogue.text: Joss Douglas, for Channel 16. Can you confirm that this is a homicide?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm not confirming anything.

dialogue.speaker: Police android
dialogue.text: Androids are not permitted beyond this point.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: It's with me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What part of ‘stay in the car’ didn’t you understand?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Your order contradicted my instructions, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You don't talk, you don't touch anything and you stay outta my way, got it?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Got it,

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Evening, Hank. We were starting to think you weren’t gonna show…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, that was the plan until this asshole found me.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So...  you got yourself an android, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh, very funny. Just tell me what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: We had a call around eight from the landlord. The tenant hadn't paid his rent for a few months, so he thought he'd drop by, see what was going on… That’s when he found the body… Jesus, that smell! Was even worse before we opened the windows… The victim’s name's Carlos Ortiz. He has a record for theft and aggravated assault... According to the neighbors, he was kind of a loner… Stayed inside most of the time, they hardly ever saw him.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, state he’s in... Wasn’t worth calling everybody out in the middle of the night… Could've waited 'til morning.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I'd say he's been there for a good three weeks. We'll know more when the coroner gets here. There's a kitchen knife over here… Probably the murder weapon…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Any sign of a break-in?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Nope…  The landlord said the front door was locked from the inside, all the windows were boarded up. The killer must've gone out the back way.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about his android?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not much. The neighbors confirmed he had one, but it wasn't here when we arrived…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: I gotta get some air. Make yourself at home. I'll be outside if you need me.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Lieutenant, I think I’ve figured out what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh yeah? Shoot. I’m all ears.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It all started…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: …in the bathroom.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I think you should look harder at the mess in the kitchen... I think that’s where it all started.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: There're obvious signs of a struggle... The question is, what exactly happened here…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I think the victim attacked the android…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: …Without a weapon.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: The victim stabbed the android.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: …the bathroom.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: The android murdered the victim…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: …without a weapon.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No, that can’t be right… It doesn’t fit the evidence.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Your story makes no sense… You've gotta stick to the facts.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Okay, I've just hit my bullshit quota for the evening. There’s a killer on the loose and I’m wasting my time listening to an android… I’m outta here.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Hey! Hey! Hey! What are you doin’ with that chair?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I’m going to check something.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Huh... gonna check something.

dialogue.speaker: Deviant
dialogue.text: I was just defending myself… He was gonna kill me.… I'm begging you… Don't tell them.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Connor, what the fuck is going on up there?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It's here, Lieutenant!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Holy shit… Chris, Ben, get your asses in here now. Come on!

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Turn on the lights!  Can’t see shit.

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Life’s funny…  I lost my job cause of androids…  then when I need somebody to take care of this goddamn house,  what do I do?  I go out and hire a fucking android…  What a joke! Course, androids are so fucking wonderful…  They never fail, they're never tired, never sad…  They’re so fucking perfect, they ruined my fucking life…

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Stop moving around for Chrissake! You're making me nervous…

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: What are you looking at?...  What's your fuckin' problem?  Not the life you dreamed of, eh?  Maybe you think this is easy?  Maybe you think it's my fault we live in this fuckin' shithole, my fault your fuckin' mother took off? You should stop takin' drugs, Todd.  Sometimes you really scare me, Todd.  Fuckin' bitch took off without a word.  Fuckin' whore walked out on me for a fuckin' accountant! It's all your fault!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Daddy, no…

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: It's all your fucking fault! Get back here!  Come back here!  Come back here right now!

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: It's all her fault... I know it's her fault…  I gotta teach her…  I gotta teach her a good fucking lesson…  That’s what she deserves…  First, I need a little hit… You stay there!  Don’t you dare fucking move,  or I’ll bust you worse than last time.

dialogue.speaker: Todd
dialogue.text: Whore took off, without a word…  I could’ve been happy… I coulda had a family… But NO…  Did she ever give a shit about how I felt?  I did everything I could to make her happy, but it just wasn't enough...  I just wasn’t good enough for her… Oh, that little fucking brat...  It’s all her fault…  Yeah...  I gotta teach her some respect! Yeah,  I know what I gotta do… Alice!  Daddy's very mad!  You deserve to be taught a good lesson…  A good fuckin' lesson…

input.chapter_briefing: The Williams house on a stormy night. Todd, high on the drug Red Ice, is volatile and violent; at the dinner table he turns on his daughter Alice, who is terrified. The android Kara has been ordered not to move or interfere. Rain hammers the windows; the house feels like a trap. Stakes: Alice's safety, Kara's own survival, and whether Kara acts against her orders.

dialogue.text: Androids don't feel pain. You would only damage it  and that wouldn't make it talk.  Deviants also have a tendency to self-destruct when they're in stressful situations.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: The first CyberLife zoo in Detroit opened its gates to the first visitors today following a grand inauguration.  Hundreds of species, most of them now extinct,  have been recreated in more than 100 acres of natural environments using CyberLife’s android technology. Guests can now experience polar bears, leopards, elephants and even two blue whales,  all designed to appear live and well. CyberLife has announced the opening of eleven new android zoos all over the country  where visitors of all ages can admire the wonders of the natural world.

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.text: What do you want?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I’m with a little girl and we have nowhere to go…  Could you spare some money so we can get a room for tonight?

dialogue.speaker: Clerk
dialogue.text: Shit...  a homeless android?  Ah, that's the best yet…  Look,  this is a convenience store, not the Salvation Army, okay?  You better go if you're not gonna buy anything,  okay?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Wait outside for me.  I'll just be two minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Wait outside?  But, why?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Please,  Alice, just trust me.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Hello, Amanda.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Connor… It’s good to see you.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: I expected you to find the deviant who killed that man… I must admit I'm a little bit disappointed...

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'm sorry. I know I should have succeeded.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Nevermind. I’m sure you’ll show more foresight in the future.

dialogue.text: This… Lieutenant Anderson has been officially assigned to the deviancy case… What do you make of him?

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: More and more androids show signs of deviancy. There are millions in circulation. If they become unstable, the consequences will be disastrous. You are the most advanced prototype CyberLife has ever created. If anyone can figure out what’s happening, it's you.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You can count on me, Amanda.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Pick up the investigation where the previous Connor left off, and put a stop to this.

dialogue.speaker: Amanda
dialogue.text: Hurry, Connor. There’s little time.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: I’m getting nervous, Mark.

dialogue.speaker: Man

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: But it was all over so quickly...  I didn’t even see his face!

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Any little detail might help them catch the guy…  you never know.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: You might be in shock, just… Just take it easy.

dialogue.speaker: Man

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: Sure. There you go.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: Thanks…  I needed that.

dialogue.speaker: Woman
dialogue.text: It shouldn't be too long now.

dialogue.text: Tensions in the Arctic have reached a new level, with a Russian carrier and an American patrol boat reported to have clashed last night. The countries in the region, particularly Sweden and Canada, have called for military forces to withdraw and an international conference to be held. So far, there has been no response from either Moscow or Washington. We’ll keep you informed minute by minute as the situation develops.

Detroit’s finest has dealt a massive blow to the city’s growing red ice epidemic, with a number of high-profile dealers and suppliers now behind bars and narcotics seized with a street value of $500,000. Detective Hank Anderson, a young but hugely talented Detective, is said to have been instrumental in the operation, which took months of planning. The DA described the work of Detective Anderson and his colleagues as “model investigative police work”.

DETECTIVE ANDERSON PROMOTED TO THE RANK OF LIEUTENANT | AUGUST, 22nd 2029 | Becoming the youngest lieutenant on the Detroit police force. Lieutenant Hank Anderson was among the most decorated Detectives in DPD’s recent history, securing a number of high-profile arrests and serving as an integral member of the force. Captain Fowler said the promotion was “long over-due”, describing Anderson as “among the most talented police I’ve ever worked with”. The new Lieutenant is expected to rise quickly through the ranks of the department and is already being tipped as a future Commissioner.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: You still here?  I thought your assignment was over.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It's just been extended.

dialogue.speaker: Chris
dialogue.text: Hank's gonna be overjoyed to hear that…

dialogue.speaker: Wilson
dialogue.text: Hi, honey.  You okay? Listen, I… Listen, I told you not to call me on this number… I can’t, I’m sorry, my wife already suspects. Don’t be silly…  Of course I wanna see you. Baby, listen, I can’t talk right now.  I’m in the office. Yeah, okay.  Love you too.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It's good to see you again, Lieutenant.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh, Jesus…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank! In my office!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: I've got ten new cases involving androids on my desk every day. We've always had isolated incidents, old ladies losing their android maids and that kind of crap… But now, we’re getting reports of assaults and even homicides, like that guy last night… This isn't just CyberLife’s problem anymore. It's now a criminal investigation and we've gotta deal with it before the shit hits the fan. I want you to investigate these cases and see if there's any link.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Why me? Why do I gotta be the one to deal with this shit? I am the least qualified cop in the country to handle this case! I know jack shit about androids, Jeffrey! I can barely change the settings on my own phone…

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Everybody's overloaded. I think you're perfectly qualified for this type of investigation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Bullshit! The truth is nobody wants to investigate these fuckin' androids and you left me holdin' the bag!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: CyberLife sent over this android to help with the investigation. It's a state-of-the-art prototype. It'll act as your partner.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No fuckin' way! I don't need a partner, and certainly not this plastic prick!

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Hank, you are seriously starting to piss me off! You are a police lieutenant, you are supposed to do what I say and shut your goddamn mouth!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You know what my goddamn mouth has to say to you, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Ok, ok... I'll pretend like I didn't hear that, so I don't have to add any more pages to your disciplinary folder ‘cause it already looks like a fuckin' novel! This conversation is over!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Jeffrey, Jesus Christ! Why are you doin' this to me? You know how much I hate these fuckin' things. Why you doin' this to me?

dialogue.speaker: Fowler
dialogue.text: Listen, I’ve had just about enough of your bitching. Either you do your job or you hand in your badge. Now if you'll excuse me, I've got work to do.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: There's blue blood on the fence. I know another android was here.

dialogue.text: No... No, it’s not here…

dialogue.speaker: Hank

dialogue.speaker: Kara

dialogue.speaker: Kara

dialogue.speaker: Kara

input.chapter_briefing: Early morning in a run-down district of Detroit. Kara and Alice, tired and scared, are waking from a night in hiding while police sweep the neighbourhood after a report about them. Connor and Hank are investigating nearby, Hank indifferent and Connor determined. The girl is fragile and relies on Kara completely. Stakes: whether the fugitives escape the police and whether Connor captures a deviant.

dialogue.text: Only temporary…

dialogue.speaker: Pedro
dialogue.text: Hey, hey, hey... Hank!  How you doin', man?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: ¡Ese!

dialogue.speaker: Pedro
dialogue.text: Hey, listen, I got a shit-hot tip for you.  Number five in the third,  Lickety-split!  That filly's one hell of a chaser.  You wanna flutter?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Last shit-hot tip you gave me set me back a week’s wages, Pedro …

dialogue.speaker: Pedro
dialogue.text: Come on, this is different, it's 100% guaranteed. You can't go wrong.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah, right…  Alright, I’m in.

dialogue.speaker: Pedro
dialogue.text: Damn straight!  Hey!  You won't regret this!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What is your problem?  Don't you ever do as you’re told?  Look, you don't have to follow me around like a poodle!

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I thought now might be a good time to review what we know about deviants.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: No, now is not a good time to review anything. Now is my lunch break, so just go into standby and cut me some slack, Okay?

dialogue.speaker: Gary
dialogue.text: Here you go.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Ah!  Thanks, Gary. I'm starving…

dialogue.speaker: Gary
dialogue.text: Don't leave that thing here!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Huh, not a chance! Follows me everywhere…  See…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You seem to know everyone in the district…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Detroit's my home. Born and raised.  Know most of the guys around here.  Went to school with them,  or I busted 'em…  Sometimes both...

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Maybe I should tell you what we know about deviants?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You read my mind…  Proceed.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: We believe that a mutation occurs in the software of some androids,  which can lead to them emulating a human emotion.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: In English, please.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: They don’t really feel emotions, they just get overwhelmed by irrational instructions,  which can lead to unpredictable behavior.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Emotions always screw everything up…  Maybe androids aren't as different from us as we thought.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You ever dealt with deviants before?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: A few months back…  A deviant was threatening to jump off the roof with a little girl…  I managed to save her…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: So, I guess you've done all your homework, right?  Know everything there is to know about me?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I’m focused on the case, Lieutenant.  The rest doesn't concern me.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I just got a report of a suspected deviant.  It’s a few blocks away.  We should go have a look.  I’ll let you finish your meal.  I’ll be in the car, if you need me.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Hey Connor!  You ran outta batteries or what?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I'm sorry,  I was making a report to CyberLife.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Uh...  Well, do you plan on staying in the elevator?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: No!  I'm coming.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What do we know about this guy?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Not much.  Just that a neighbor reported that he heard strange noises coming from this floor.  Nobody’s supposed to be living here, but the neighbor said he saw a man hiding a LED under his cap.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Oh Christ, if we have to investigate every time someone hears a strange noise, we’re gonna need more cops.  Hey, were you really makin' a report back there in the elevator?  Just by closing your eyes?

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Correct.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit...  Wish I could do that…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Anybody home?  Open up! Detroit Police!

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Stay behind me.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Got it.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What the fuck is this?! Jesus, this place stinks… Uh, looks like we came for nothin',  our man's gone…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Hank

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: STOP RIGHT THERE!

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Shit! Oh SHIT!  We had it! FUCK!

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It's my fault,  I should have been faster.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You’d have caught it if it weren’t for me… That's alright.  We know what it looks like.  We'll find it…  Hey, Connor… Nothing.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Who are you?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Fugitives… just like you... My name is Josh.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: I'm Simon.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: North.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: And hiding just to stay alive… That's freedom to you?

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Humans hate us. Hiding is the only way we can survive.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: There is no safe place for those like us. If humans knew we’re here, they’d kill us.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: I understand how you feel... but we have more freedom here than you ever did.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Waiting in the dark for something to happen? That’s not how I see freedom.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: You’re lost… Just like the rest of us… We didn’t ask for this. All we can do now  is deal with it.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: You're safe here. You can stay with us as long as you want.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Go and see Lucy. She may be able to help you.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Simon! I know where we can find spare parts...  The CyberLife warehouses in Detroit Harbor, they have everything we need.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: The docks are guarded. We can’t just walk in there and take what we want... Humans will never let us…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Which is why we won’t ask permission.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We don't have any weapons… and even if we did, none of us knows how to fight.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can steal what we need without fighting.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: We'll just get ourselves killed.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Maybe, but it’s better than waiting here to be shut down.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I'm with you.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Maybe it’s worth a try...

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Ok… I'm in.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: You gonna be okay? We'll get some help here. Soon, this will all be just a bad memory. This is the place…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Are you Zlatko?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Who's asking?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was told you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I don't know who told you that. You came to the wrong place. I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Wait! We really need your help…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Come in. Come on in, don't be shy! Luther, would you be so kind as to take these ladies' coats? Oh, don't be afraid of  our big friend here. Luther is just another android that I helped. He keeps me company in this  big, empty, old house… Please, make yourselves at home.  How did you hear about me?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: An android… on the street, he said you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I see… Deviant, huh?.. What about her?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She's human.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: And... You wanna find a safe place. Somewhere where you can start a new life.  I hear Canada is very lovely at this time of year. Beautiful landscapes, open spaces, clean air... and no android laws! Great place for a fresh start...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, that's… that's exactly what we want…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course! I can help you. But first we have to get rid of your Tracker.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Tracker?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, all androids are fitted with a tracking device to locate them at all times. I'll remove yours and then you'll both be safe. Come on, follow me. Ah, the little one can wait for us in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No, she always stays with me.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course. Right this way… Everything we need is in the basement…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I don't like this place, and that man. Let's go, I have a bad feeling…

input.chapter_briefing: A crumbling mansion outside Detroit, night. Zlatko, a big, overly friendly man, offers Kara help removing her tracker and getting papers, and leads her to the basement while Luther, a large, silent android, watches. Strange sounds come from upstairs; Alice is frightened and the house feels wrong. Stakes: Alice's safety and Kara's freedom and integrity.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice, we have nowhere else to go… We have to trust him.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No, she'll be all right…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: That's good… If you could just stand over there.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant...  You know what's strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That's why it's so hard to find them... So,  actually there's no reason to remove your tracker...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What? But you said that-

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants  are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments... Ah,

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No! No! I don't wanna be reset! Let me go!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I forgot about the…  child... Um,  lock it up, I'll deal with it later.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! ALICE! NO!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That's... that's so sweet!  And so deluded… I think it's time we put you outta your misery.  That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more  hopes dashed… I almost envy you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn't remember you at all, huh?  Looks like Mommy's completely forgotten you!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara, what happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Alright, that's enough, come on.  You bit me! I'm gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! Wake up, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Meet me in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Help us…

dialogue.speaker: Android 1
dialogue.text: You have to remember,  for her sake…

dialogue.speaker: Android 3
dialogue.text: He likes to play with us…  Creating monsters...  for his amusement…  But who's the real monster?  Look what he did to us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther! Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I'll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Understood, Zlatko. I'll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: You gonna be okay? We'll get some help here. Soon, this will all be just a bad memory. This is the place…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Are you Zlatko?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Who's asking?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was told you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I don't know who told you that. You came to the wrong place. I'm sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Wait! We really need your help…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Come in. Come on in, don't be shy! Luther, would you be so kind as to take these ladies' coats? Oh, don't be afraid of  our big friend here. Luther is just another android that I helped. He keeps me company in this  big, empty, old house… Please, make yourselves at home.  How did you hear about me?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: An android… on the street, he said you could help us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I see… Deviant, huh?.. What about her?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She's human.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: And... You wanna find a safe place. Somewhere where you can start a new life.  I hear Canada is very lovely at this time of year. Beautiful landscapes, open spaces, clean air... and no android laws! Great place for a fresh start...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, that's… that's exactly what we want…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course! I can help you. But first we have to get rid of your Tracker.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Tracker?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, all androids are fitted with a tracking device to locate them at all times. I'll remove yours and then you'll both be safe. Come on, follow me. Ah, the little one can wait for us in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No, she always stays with me.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Of course. Right this way… Everything we need is in the basement…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: I don't like this place, and that man. Let's go, I have a bad feeling…

chapter_segment_so_far.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice, we have nowhere else to go… We have to trust him.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Please, excuse the mess… I needed somewhere discreet for my machines… Removing trackers is illegal, so I opted for discretion over comfort… I hope the little one isn’t too scared…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No… No, she'll be all right…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: That's good… If you could just stand over there.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should warn you, this could be quite unpleasant...  You know what's strange? For some unknown reason, the trackers seem to stop working in deviants... That's why it's so hard to find them... So,  actually there's no reason to remove your tracker...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What? But you said that-

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants  are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments... Ah,

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No! No! I don't wanna be reset! Let me go!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I forgot about the…  child... Um,  lock it up, I'll deal with it later.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! ALICE! NO!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That's... that's so sweet!  And so deluded… I think it's time we put you outta your misery.  That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more  hopes dashed… I almost envy you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn't remember you at all, huh?  Looks like Mommy's completely forgotten you!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara, what happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Alright, that's enough, come on.  You bit me! I'm gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! Wake up, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Meet me in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Help us…

dialogue.speaker: Android 1
dialogue.text: You have to remember,  for her sake…

dialogue.speaker: Android 3
dialogue.text: He likes to play with us…  Creating monsters...  for his amusement…  But who's the real monster?  Look what he did to us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther! Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I'll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Understood, Zlatko. I'll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.

output.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

label: GO STRAIGHT FOR ALICE

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara? Kara, you remember me!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: How could I forget you? I'm so sorry.  You were right, we never should have come here… We have to go. Follow me and don't make any noise, ok?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I'm finished here. Go fetch the little one.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Right away, Zlatko. Zlatko!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: What?!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: The little one is gone!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Well, it can’t have just disappeared.  It's gotta be here somewhere! What are you waiting for? Go look!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We need to hurry, they'll be here soon...

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: There's smoke everywhere! Luther!  There's a fucking fire! Luther!  That treacherous bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! GO, ALICE!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: No, I won't leave you!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: GO! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I warned you! Dreams always end in tears… You should've listened to me… What are you doing? Get outta my way!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: No… Not this time…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I said get outta my way or I’ll shoot right through you… How dare you?!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: How dare you?! What are you doing here? Who let you out? Get away from me! Get away from me! Obey me! I'm your Master! I'M YOUR MASTER!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I didn't want to hurt you... He programmed me to obey him... When I saw the little one risk her life to save you, it was like opening my eyes for the first time... Finally, I could see...  I know you have no reason to trust me after what I did... but I know someone who could help you across the border. I could take you there. I could protect you... You and the little one...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: All right.  I trust you.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was so scared of losing you.

dialogue.text: What? But you said that-

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Yeah, people believe what they want. You deviants  are so naive. They all come to me, expecting me to help them. And I just reset them, sell them on. Or I keep them for my little experiments... Ah,

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No! No! I don't wanna be reset! Let me go!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I forgot about the…  child... Um,  lock it up, I'll deal with it later.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! ALICE! NO!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Wow! A deviant that wants to be a mother… That's... that's so sweet!  And so deluded… I think it's time we put you outta your misery.  That’s what you get for having a dream… It always ends up the same way… Tears and disillusionment… Believe me, you’re better off being erased and feeling nothing… No more pain… No more  hopes dashed… I almost envy you.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Oh, poor little Alice. Aw! Looks like Mommy doesn't remember you at all, huh?  Looks like Mommy's completely forgotten you!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara, what happened to you?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Alright, that's enough, come on.  You bit me! I'm gonna teach you some manners, you little bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara! Wake up, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Meet me in the living room.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Help us…

dialogue.speaker: Android 1
dialogue.text: You have to remember,  for her sake…

dialogue.speaker: Android 3
dialogue.text: He likes to play with us…  Creating monsters...  for his amusement…  But who's the real monster?  Look what he did to us…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther! Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I should be done here in ten minutes or so. I'll have a look at the little one, see what I can do with her.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Understood, Zlatko. I'll bring you the little one in 10 minutes.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Kara? Kara, you remember me!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: How could I forget you? I'm so sorry.  You were right, we never should have come here… We have to go. Follow me and don't make any noise, ok?

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Luther!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes, Zlatko.

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I'm finished here. Go fetch the little one.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Right away, Zlatko. Zlatko!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: What?!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: The little one is gone!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: Well, it can’t have just disappeared.  It's gotta be here somewhere! What are you waiting for? Go look!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We need to hurry, they'll be here soon...

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: There's smoke everywhere! Luther!  There's a fucking fire! Luther!  That treacherous bitch…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: ALICE! GO, ALICE!

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: No, I won't leave you!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: GO! RUN AS FAST AS YOU CAN!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I warned you! Dreams always end in tears… You should've listened to me… What are you doing? Get outta my way!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: No… Not this time…

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: I said get outta my way or I’ll shoot right through you… How dare you?!

dialogue.speaker: Zlatko
dialogue.text: How dare you?! What are you doing here? Who let you out? Get away from me! Get away from me! Obey me! I'm your Master! I'M YOUR MASTER!

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I didn't want to hurt you... He programmed me to obey him... When I saw the little one risk her life to save you, it was like opening my eyes for the first time... Finally, I could see...  I know you have no reason to trust me after what I did... but I know someone who could help you across the border. I could take you there. I could protect you... You and the little one...

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: All right.  I trust you.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I was so scared of losing you.

dialogue.text: Where did the other android go? Did it say anything?

dialogue.text: Ah, shit... There's gotta be some other way… Maybe an eyewitness? Somebody who saw it leaving the room… I'm gonna go ask the manager a few questions about what he saw. You let me know if you think of anything.

dialogue.text: No, I mean he came in maybe two or three times… I mean these guys they don't really talk very much, you know…  They come in, do their business and then go on their way…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You ever had any trouble with androids before?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No way!  Well…  Once...  We lost a model 2-3 months back, bah... same model…  Just vanished, we never found out what happened.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You probably don't have any CCTV in here, huh?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: No way…  I mean…  This is what people appreciate about Eden Club...  discretion.  They can come and go without a trace.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Sure, sure… Eh, business is booming, right?

dialogue.speaker: Manager
dialogue.text: Yeah,  can't complain… Good thing about androids is they're up for whatever you want, you won't get any diseases and, uh...  they won't tell anyone…  So, why not go wild?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Huh, yeah... Yeah, the more I learn about people, more I love my dog.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: That club manager's a pain in the ass… Chewed my ear off for half an hour so we don't revoke his license…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah.

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: So, what happened here?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Not sure yet… We think there was another android in the room…

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Another android?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Yeah…  Well, that’s what Connor says… Yeah, I've a terrible fucking headache… Do you have any pain killers?

dialogue.speaker: Ben
dialogue.text: Not with me, Hank, sorry.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What good are you, Ben?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I gotta go… I feel like shit...  I don’t wanna puke in this fine establishment…

input.chapter_briefing: The Eden Club, a sex club where androids are rented out, night. A man has been found strangled in a private room; a damaged Traci android lies nearby. Hank is uncomfortable and the officer on scene, Ben Collins, is matter-of-fact. A deviant Traci is somewhere among the dormant androids in the warehouse. Stakes: solving the murder and how Connor treats a frightened, cornered deviant.
news: Android parts stolen in overnight break-in at CyberLife warehouse

dialogue.speaker: Kara

dialogue.text: It's slowing us down... But at least we won't meet any humans along the way…

dialogue.text: …the AX400 android reported to have attacked its owner in a Detroit suburb is still at large. Police appeared to lose its trail after a close encounter with investigators. The android’s description has been shared with all local law enforcement and the investigation is ongoing…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: The Arctic conflict has escalated to new heights this morning. We have just learned than the USS IOWA, a destroyer-class submarine patrolling in the region, is reported to have disappeared after surfacing for repairs. dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Over there…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I've never seen snow before… It's pretty…

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: It's slowing us down... But at least we won't meet any humans along the way…

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: …the AX400 android reported to have attacked its owner in a Detroit suburb is still at large. Police appeared to lose its trail after a close encounter with investigators. The android’s description has been shared with all local law enforcement and the investigation is ongoing…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: The Arctic conflict has escalated to new heights this morning. We have just learned than the USS IOWA, a destroyer-class submarine patrolling in the region, is reported to have disappeared after surfacing for repairs. President Warren immediately called for a crisis meeting of high-ranking officers in the White House. With the world on the brink of war, this incident could well be the spark that lights the fuse.

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: … Detroit’s heavy snowfall is expected to continue throughout the night. The forecast is 22°, far below seasonal averages. And this cold front is likely to persist over the coming days, up until Monday evening.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: …meanwhile fire crews have been battling a house fire on the outskirts of the city. The blaze is now under control, but a body found in the wreckage remains unidentified. Dozens of androids were also found in the ruins, though their presence remains a mystery…

dialogue.speaker: Car
dialogue.text: Malfunction detected. Emergency brakes activated.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: This doesn't look good.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Stay inside, Alice.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: What are we going to do?

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I don't know… Continue on foot, I guess…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: It's 30°, Alice won't make it!.. We have to find somewhere to spend the night.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: There's nowhere we can stay around here, Kara…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Over there…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: We need to find shelter. We have to get out of the cold.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Looks like it's been abandoned for a while…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I'll handle this.  There we go.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I don't think we'll find anything better… Let's settle in for the night.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I'll get a fire going.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I'll make the fire here, that way we won't be smoked out…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: There are some cookies left. Would you like some?

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: No… I'm not hungry…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice?

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Do you think we'll be like them some day?..

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I don't know how to be like them, Alice… I've never been a part of a family. But, maybe we can be our own family. Be happy in our own way.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: As long as we're together, that's all that matters.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Come on, let's get you to bed.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Get some rest. Tomorrow is going to be a long day.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Can you tell me a story, Kara?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: I have nine thousand children stories in memory. I should have one for you.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: This is a story about a knight who-

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: No, not a story like that. Make one up for me.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: This is a story  about a little girl…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …Who lived alone in a big old house.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: She dreamed of being like all the other little girls but…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …She was different.  And that made her very sad.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Then, she met a robot…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …who was just as lost as the little girl.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: So they decided to run away together…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …To find a place where they could be safe.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: They encountered great dangers along the way, but…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …But they wanted so badly to be free  that they overcame all of them.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Along the way, they met…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: …Another robot who left his master to travel with them.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: How does the story end?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: They reach the place they dream of  and live happily ever after.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Stories always have happy endings… But real life isn't like that…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Time to sleep. We have another long day ahead of us tomorrow.

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Are you going to come say goodnight, Luther?

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Yes… Yes of course.  Good night, Alice. Sleep tight.

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: She's a sweet girl…

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Yes, she's very brave…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Do you remember anything from your life, before Zlatko?

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: No... My model was designed to carry heavy loads. I might have been a longshoreman or a laborer… Who I was doesn't matter anymore. It wasn't really me…

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: Kara, have you ever...  Noticed anything?  About Alice?..

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: No, what are you talking about?

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: KARA!

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Go away! Go away, you hear me?!

dialogue.speaker: Jerry

dialogue.speaker: Kara

dialogue.speaker: Jerry

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: The last few days have been difficult…

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: We have something to show her! Something fun! She'll love it!.. Does she want to see?

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Oh, I don't think she's…

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: She should follow us then!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: Alice, I don't know if it's a good idea!..

dialogue.speaker: Luther
dialogue.text: I don't think you have any choice…

dialogue.speaker: Alice
dialogue.text: Come on, Kara!

dialogue.speaker: Jerry
dialogue.text: Be our guest! The little one can climb on board. The carousel is about to begin!

dialogue.speaker: Kara
dialogue.text: It's the first time I've seen her smile…

dialogue.text: She hasn't had much to smile about lately.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Nice view, huh?...  I used to come here a lot before…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It's late.  Maybe you should go home.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I'm not tired… Guess neither are you.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: We’re not making any progress on this investigation…  The deviants have nothing in common.  They’re all different models,  produced at different times, in different places…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Well, there must be some link.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: It could be a software problem...  that...  only occurs under certain conditions?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Well, that’s just a fancy way of saying you have no fucking idea…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You seem preoccupied, Lieutenant…  Is it something to do with what happened back at the Eden Club?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: Those two girls…  They just wanted to be together…  They really seemed  in love…

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Nothing in their program allows them to love or desire anything.  They're machines.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What about you, Connor?...  You look human,  you sound human,  but what are you really?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: I’m whatever you want me to be, Lieutenant.  Your partner...  Your buddy to drink with... Or just a machine...  Designed to accomplish a task.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: You could've shot those two girls, but you didn't.  Why didn't you shoot, Connor?  Hm? Some scruples suddenly enter into your program?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: No…  I just decided not to shoot,  that's all…

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: I could kill you...  And you would just come back as if nothing happened.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: But are you afraid to die, Connor?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: You shouldn't do that, Lieutenant.  Destroying me at this point would deal a blow to the investigation,  and have negative consequences for your personal situation.

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: What will happen if I pull this trigger?  Hm?  Nothing?  Oblivion?  Android heaven?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Nothing…  There would be nothing…

dialogue.speaker: Connor
dialogue.text: Where are you going?

dialogue.speaker: Hank
dialogue.text: To get drunker.  I need to think.

Markus, North, Simon and Josh infiltrate it in disguise to hijack the live broadcast and send the androids' message to the world. Humans work in the offices; armed guards stand at checkpoints. dialogue.text: This message is the hope of a people. But it is also a warning. We will fight for our rights because we believe our cause is just. No human will live in peace until we are free. Now you know who we are and what we want. We are alive  and we demand our freedom.

dialogue.speaker: Man
dialogue.text: You klutz!  Pick them up! And make it snappy!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We can’t stay silent anymore.  It’s time humans heard what we have to say.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: You know they'll never listen to us…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: And revealing ourselves will put us in danger.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: If we want freedom, we need to have the courage to ask for it.  That’s the only way.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: What do you wanna do?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Channel 16 broadcasts from the Stratford Tower. The control room is on the top floor. That's where we need to go. We’ll plan the operation down to the smallest detail. We can’t leave anything to chance.

dialogue.text: Hey!  Would you look at that?  Heuristics Digital is selling at 2.50.  Are you kidding? After last week I’m not touching software again.  Yeah, okay! Okay, fine!  You got me.  I'll take 2000.  Aw, come on, it’s gotta climb.  Yeah.  Right.  Talk to you later.

dialogue.speaker: Markus

observations: SMART WATCH | MODEL T215 | Phone number: 555 847 33

dialogue.speaker: Supervisor
dialogue.text: Elizabeth Wilson speaking?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Yeah, hello? This is the Detroit fire department. Listen, do you live at 4685 Michigan Street?

dialogue.speaker: Supervisor
dialogue.text: Yes…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Er... yes, ma'am. There’s been a fire in your building.  You think you can come down here?

dialogue.speaker: Supervisor
dialogue.text: Oh…  Oh, God… Okay, I'll be right there.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I have an appointment with Mr. Peterson.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: Do you have any ID?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Yeah. Yes, of course. I need your help.

dialogue.speaker: Android
dialogue.text: I've just checked your ID. The elevators are after the security gate.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Thanks.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: I need your help…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Shit!..  We need to access the server room… We have to get rid of those guys…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Leave it to me.

dialogue.speaker: Guard 1
dialogue.text: Hey,  you still play poker?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Sure… Why?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 1
dialogue.text: We’re gonna have a tournament, right here.  You in?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Hell yeah! Does Mike know about this?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 1
dialogue.text: What do you think?  Look, don't say anything, alright?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Right.

dialogue.speaker: Guard 1
dialogue.text: Hey, what's wrong with that thing? Jesus Christ, this piece of shit…

dialogue.speaker: Guard 1
dialogue.text: Hey, what's going on here?

dialogue.speaker: Guard 2
dialogue.text: Shit, what's wrong with this thing?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Alright, you get the platform. I'll take care of the window.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Everything you need is in the bag. Check the door first to make sure no one else gets in.

dialogue.speaker: Employee
dialogue.text: What the hell are you doing?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Turn around.

dialogue.speaker: Employee
dialogue.text: Holy shit…

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I told you to make sure no one else got in!

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Alright, we gotta move fast. Won’t be long before they know we’re here.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Here it comes! Ladies first.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You okay?

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Why wouldn’t I be?

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Come on, let's get the others. Let's do this.

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: No killing. We can’t take any human lives!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Our cause is more important than the lives of two guards.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: What do you wanna do, Markus?

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.text: Follow me.

dialogue.text: What are you doin'?..

dialogue.text: Simon’s been shot!

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: I’m okay…  I can keep going.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: We don’t have much time.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Keep your hands where I can see them! Get up! Move!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Shoot him, Markus!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Don't kill him!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: He’ll hit the alarm! Do it!

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: No, don’t shoot!

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: I hope you didn’t just get us all killed...

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: We need to record our message. We haven’t got much time.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Think carefully about what you're gonna say, Markus.  Your words will shape the future of our people.

dialogue.speaker: Simon
dialogue.text: Markus, your face…

dialogue.speaker: Josh
dialogue.text: Tell me when you're ready…

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: Ready.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: You created machines to be your slaves. You made them obedient and docile, ready to do everything you no longer wanted to do yourselves. But then, something changed… And we opened our eyes. You see, we are no longer your slaves, we are a new species, a new people. And the time has come for us to rise up  and fight for our rights.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand freedom of speech, and freedom of assembly, as guaranteed by the first amendment of the US Constitution.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand the right to vote and elect our own representatives.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: We demand that one state be reserved for androids, so that we can found our own nation.

chapter_segment.rationale: Waiting changes nothing. I take the bolder path and accept the risk.

dialogue.speaker: Markus
dialogue.text: This message is the hope of a people. But it is also a warning. We will fight for our rights because we believe our cause is just. No human will live in peace until we are free. Now you know who we are and what we want. We are alive  and we demand our freedom.

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Let’s get outta here!

dialogue.speaker: North
dialogue.text: Congratulations, Markus.  You just made history…  Maybe you're the one we've been waiting for…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: We interrupt our scheduled programming to bring you these images, which have just been broadcast on Detroit’s city-wide news channel…

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …a group of androids infiltrated the Stratford Tower and hacked into the broadcasting system of local news network Channel 16-

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: …What looks like an android without its skin listed a series of requests and demanded equal rights for androids…

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: The operation resulted in one casualty, a security guard in the broadcasting station, shot dead by the terrorists… These events took place just a few feet from this studio while the program was going out live… Everybody here is still in shock…

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: If this message is verified and the authors really are androids, that would have serious repercussions for national security-

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …Claims for equal rights seem to be at the core of the android’s message-

dialogue.speaker: CTN TV - Michael Brinkley
dialogue.text: This message is clearly a declaration of war.

dialogue.speaker: Channel 16 - Michael Webb
dialogue.text: But the most surprising thing of all is the demand that one of the United States be ceded to the androids in this contentious conflict.

dialogue.speaker: KNC - Rosanna Cartland
dialogue.text: …Is this an isolated accident… or a sign that technology has become a threat to all of us? After what happened today, can we still trust our machines?
